name: Standing hip CARs
description: Controlled Articular Rotations for the hip — the widest possible active circle the hip can own, one leg at a time. Active mobility, not a passive stretch.
setup: Stand tall on one leg, hand on a wall for balance
Drive the other knee up to the front as high as it will actively go
Take that knee out to the side, then rotate the hip so the heel sweeps back
Extend the leg behind, then reverse the circle
cues: Move the hip, not the spine — ribs stay stacked over pelvis, no arching
Go slow at the edges of the circle; that end-range is where the work is
Own the range actively; don't fling the leg

name: 90/90 hip switch
description: Seated 90/90 rotations train hip internal and external rotation together — the exact range that limits cutting and change of direction.
setup: Sit with front leg bent 90° in front, back leg bent 90° out to the side
Keep the chest tall and both sit-bones as heavy as you can
Rotate both knees over to the other side, lifting through the hips
Pause when the trailing knee lifts — that's your internal-rotation edge
cues: Internal rotation is the goal — the trailing hip that wants to lift
Hinge forward over the front shin for a deeper external-rotation load
Slow and controlled; no bouncing

name: Cossack squat (active)
description: Wide lateral squat that opens the adductors and loads one hip deep while the other leg extends — mobility trained under your own control.
setup: Stand wide, feet a little turned out
Shift into one hip, sitting deep, keeping that whole foot down
The other leg stays long, toes up
Pause at the bottom, then shift smoothly to the other side
cues: Keep the working heel planted — no rolling onto the toes
Knee tracks over the foot, never caving in
Own a brief pause at the bottom rather than bouncing through

name: World's greatest stretch
description: A moving lunge-plus-rotation that hits the hip flexor, adductor, and thoracic rotation in one active flow. Prime, don't stretch-and-hold.
setup: Step into a long lunge, both hands inside the front foot
Drop the back knee slightly to feel the hip flexor lengthen
Drive the inside elbow toward the floor, then rotate that arm up to the ceiling
Follow the hand with the eyes, then switch sides
cues: Rotate from the mid-back, opening the chest
Keep the front knee tracking over the foot
Move continuously — this is a prep flow, not a static hold

name: Knee-to-wall ankle rock
description: Loaded ankle dorsiflexion mobilization. Restricted dorsiflexion drives the knee inward on every squat, land, and cut — free it at the base.
setup: Face a wall in a half-kneel, front foot a few inches back from it
Drive the front knee forward over the toes to touch the wall — heel stays down
If it touches easily, slide the foot back and repeat at the new distance
Rock in and out at your end range
cues: Heel must stay glued to the floor — that's the honest range
Knee travels straight over the 2nd/3rd toe, not inward
Small, repeated rocks into the end range

name: Deep squat sit
description: Sitting in the bottom of a deep squat and actively organizing it — ankles, hips, and pelvis learning to own end-range under body weight.
setup: Squat down as far as is comfortable, heels down, holding something in front if needed
Let the hips sink between the feet
Gently press the knees out with the elbows and lift the chest
Shift side to side and rock the ankles to explore the position
cues: Heels stay down; widen the stance if they lift
Actively press knees out — don't just hang passively
Breathe into the position and relax the hips lower

name: Short-foot / tripod
description: Actively doming the arch by drawing the ball of the foot toward the heel without curling the toes. Wakes the intrinsic foot muscles — the base of the whole chain.
setup: Stand with the foot flat, weight through the tripod: big-toe ball, little-toe ball, heel
Without curling the toes, draw the ball of the foot toward the heel so the arch lifts
Hold the dome, toes long and relaxed
Release slowly
cues: Toes stay long and flat — the lift comes from under the arch
Keep all three tripod points loaded
Small movement, big focus

name: Windlass big-toe press
description: Driving the big toe down (or extending it) to tension the plantar fascia and raise the arch — the windlass mechanism, the foot's own spring and the start of the foot→glute line.
setup: Stand with the foot in its tripod
Press the big toe firmly into the floor while keeping the other toes relaxed
Feel the arch rise and the plantar fascia tension
Alternate: lift and spread the toes, then set just the big toe back down first
cues: Big toe drives down, arch lifts — that's the spring loading
Don't let the arch collapse inward
Keep the heel and outer foot quiet

name: Hyperarch hold
description: Tensioning the whole foot into a locked, high-arch spring and holding it — not curling the toes, but drawing the forefoot and heel toward each other so the arch domes and the ankle stiffens as one unit. The foot-first connection the rest of the chain hangs from (HFT-inspired: train tension, not isolated toes).
setup: Stand barefoot in the tripod: big-toe ball, little-toe ball, and heel all loaded
Without clawing the toes, draw the forefoot and heel toward each other so the arch lifts and locks
Feel the whole foot and ankle stiffen into one springy unit, toes long and relaxed
Hold the tension, breathing easy; release slowly
cues: Lock the whole foot as ONE unit — this is tension, not a toe curl
Big-toe ball stays planted as the arch domes up
The ankle stiffens with the arch — one connected spring from the ground up

name: Single-leg calf isometric
description: A mid-range single-leg heel-raise hold. Builds ankle and Achilles stiffness — the stored spring you need before any hopping.
setup: Stand on one foot, fingertips on a wall for balance
Rise onto the ball of the foot to a strong mid-height position
Hold rock-steady, ankle stacked over the foot
Lower under control
cues: Push evenly through the big-toe and little-toe balls — no rolling out
Ankle doesn't wobble; build a stiff, quiet spring
Keep the arch locked (hyperarch) as you rise — carry the foot tension up the leg
Tall through the whole leg

name: Tibialis raise
description: Pulling the toes up against gravity to train the front of the shin — the balancing partner to the calf and a key brake for deceleration.
setup: Stand with the back against a wall, heels a step out from it
Keep the legs straight and lean the hips back on the wall
Pull the toes and forefoot up toward the shins as high as possible
Lower slowly under control
cues: Heels stay planted; only the forefoot lifts
Feel the burn on the front of the shin
Control the way down — don't drop

name: Banded ankle in/eversion
description: Light-band resisted ankle turns for the sides of the ankle — the stabilizers that keep the ankle honest on quick direction changes.
setup: Sit with the leg out, band looped around the forefoot and anchored to the side
Turn the sole outward against the band (eversion), then reset
Re-anchor on the other side and turn the sole inward (inversion)
Move only at the ankle
cues: Slow and deliberate — the light band is for control, not load
Keep the shin still; the motion is all foot
Full range both directions

name: Single-leg balance (quiet foot)
description: Standing on one foot and making the foot and ankle go quiet. Trains the sensory side of the base — the foot learning to feel and correct.
setup: Stand on one foot in its tripod, other knee softly lifted
Find a fixed point to look at
Let the arch and ankle make tiny corrections to stay centered
Progress by closing the eyes
cues: Hold the foot in a locked arch (hyperarch) — a quiet, domed tripod, not clawing toes
Quiet the sway — feel the corrections get smaller
Knee soft, hips level

name: Banded clamshell
description: Hip external rotation against a light band — direct glute-medius/rotator activation to feed knee control from above. Progression (the version you're using): lie with both feet braced on a wall and the outside (bottom) foot planted, then drive the top knee open against that wall feedback — more load and a more sport-shaped, weight-bearing external rotation than the floor clamshell.
setup: Lie on your side, knees bent, band above the knees, hips stacked
Keep the feet together and the pelvis still
Open the top knee by rotating the hip, without rolling the pelvis back
Lower under control
Progression (wall-supported): brace both feet on a wall with the outside foot planted, then rotate the top hip open against the wall for more load
cues: The pelvis must not rock backward — isolate the hip
Feel it in the side of the glute, not the low back
Pause at the top of each rep
Wall version: press the planted foot into the wall and rotate against it — pelvis stays quiet, drive from the glute

name: Side-lying hip abduction
description: Raising the top leg straight up in side-lying to load the glute medius through range — the abductor strength that resists the knee caving in on landing.
setup: Lie on your side, bottom leg bent, top leg straight and in line with the body
Turn the top toes slightly down toward the floor
Raise the straight top leg toward the ceiling
Lower slowly without letting the hip roll
cues: Lead with the heel, toe slightly down — targets glute medius
Keep the leg slightly behind the body, not drifting forward
No rolling back to cheat height

name: Lateral band walk
description: Stepping sideways against a light band in a quarter-squat — glute-medius under a standing, closed-chain load with the knees driving out.
setup: Band above the knees or around the ankles, sink into a quarter-squat
Step one foot out to the side, staying low
Bring the trailing foot in only partway so the band stays tensioned
Walk a set number of steps each direction
cues: Knees drive out against the band the whole time — never let them cave
Stay low and level; don't bob up and down
Feet point straight ahead

name: Copenhagen adduction (ball)
description: A side-plank with the top leg resting on the ball, lifting the bottom leg to it — the strongest adductor builder there is, scaled by lever length. No weights needed.

Start easy: keep the bottom knee bent and down (short lever)
Lift the hips so the body is straight, squeezing the bottom leg up toward the ball
Progress by straightening the bottom leg (long lever)
cues: Adductor of the down leg does the work — feel the inner thigh
Body stays in one straight line, hips high
Start with the short-lever (bent knee) version and earn the long lever

name: Adductor ball squeeze
description: Squeezing the ball between the knees in a bridge — an isometric adductor and deep-core connection that also stabilizes the pelvis.
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, the ball between the knees
Squeeze the ball firmly with both knees
Hold the squeeze and lift into a glute bridge
Keep squeezing throughout the hold
cues: Inner thighs and deep core switch on together
Ribs down, no arching the low back
Constant squeeze — don't let the ball relax

description: A held bridge that wakes the glutes and teaches hip extension driven by the glute, not the low back — the reciprocal partner that quiets an overactive psoas.

Drive through the heels and lift the hips to a straight knee-hip-shoulder line
Squeeze the glutes hard; keep the ribs down
Hold, then lower slowly

Posteriorly tilt the pelvis first, then lift — glute-driven

description: Feet up on the ball in a bridge, marching one knee toward the chest against active hip flexion — trains the psoas as a strong deep-flexion hip flexor, not something to stretch.

Keep the hips level and the ball still
Drive one knee up toward the chest, holding briefly at the top
Return and switch sides without dropping the hips

Active pull at the top of the knee drive — that's the psoas working
Slow and controlled; the challenge is anti-drop, not speed

Rotate the pelvis open toward the ceiling, then closed toward the floor
Move slowly through the rotation without the knee caving

Small, owned range beats big and sloppy

name: Wall sit (knees out)
description: A closed-chain quad isometric with the back on the wall — builds quad capacity and knee-tracking with the patella seated and safe.

Feet hip-width, weight through the mid-foot and heels
Gently press the knees outward so they track over the toes
Hold; breathe steadily
cues: Knees stay out over the 2nd toe — never let them drift in
Push the whole back into the wall
Stop the set if the kneecap feels unstable, not from burn
Depth: start partial (thighs above parallel) and earn depth over weeks — an iso builds strength mainly at the angle you hold, so deepen only as the knee stays quiet

description: A band looped behind the knees to an anchor lets you sit back into a deep knee isometric with an upright torso — heavy quad/knee load, closed chain, patella stays seated.

Sit back against the band into a squat, torso staying upright
Shins stay fairly vertical; let the band take the backward pull
Hold, driving the knees gently out
cues: Upright torso — the band supports you sitting back
Knees track out over the feet
Big quad tension without the patella feeling loose
Depth: start shallow and earn depth over weeks — the hold trains the angle you sit at, so only go deeper as the knee stays quiet

description: A held bottom of a split squat — single-leg-biased quad and hip isometric that also opens the trailing hip flexor. Closed chain, foot planted.
setup: Step into a split stance, lower until the front thigh is near parallel
Front shin vertical, weight through the front mid-foot
Trailing knee under or just behind the hip
Hold tall through the torso
cues: Front knee tracks over the foot, heel down
Squeeze the trailing glute to load the hip flexor stretch
Torso stays upright and braced
Depth: start with a shallow front-knee bend and earn depth over weeks as the knee stays stacked and quiet

name: Squat hold (parallel)
description: A free-standing squat held with the thighs toward parallel — the bilateral 'base position' of the long-duration isometric method. No wall to lean on, so the trunk and quads own the position. Build the hold time gradually; the point is a calm, braced position, not a grind. Closed chain, patella seated.
setup: Feet hip-to-shoulder width, sit back and down until the thighs are toward parallel
Shins near vertical, chest up, weight through the mid-foot
Brace the trunk and hold the position still
Breathe easy through the hold; build the duration over time
cues: Knees track out over the 2nd toe — never let them cave
Relax the face and jaw — stay calm inside the tension (don't grind or shake)
Only as deep as the knees stay quiet; shorten the hold before form breaks
Depth: start partial (thighs above parallel) and earn depth over weeks — an iso builds strength mainly at the angle you hold, so deepen gradually

name: Single-leg squat hold
description: A free (unsupported) single-leg partial-squat held still — the single-leg position of the long-duration isometric method, and the step up from the wall-supported version. Arms out and the free leg forward for balance; hold the knee stacked and quiet. Closed chain keeps the patella seated.
setup: Stand on one leg, arms out in front for balance, free leg floating forward
Sit to a comfortable single-leg partial squat (thigh toward parallel as able)
Hold with the knee tracking straight over the foot
Breathe easy; build the time only as control allows
cues: Knee stays stacked over the foot — this is the whole event
Relax and breathe — don't grind; a trembling hold means back off the depth or time
End the hold the moment it wobbles or the kneecap feels unsure
Depth: start shallow (a quarter-range is fine) and earn depth over weeks — single-leg especially, the angle you can hold quiet is the right angle to start

Stop where the hamstring and glute load up and your balance holds
Hold still, flat back, hips square

Keep the hips square — don't let the back hip open up to the ceiling
Drive the stance foot into the floor to anchor the position

Small circles you can control beat big ones you can't

Reach toward the floor while the back stays flat

Reach to the side, then behind at an angle, staying balanced
Keep the stance foot quiet the whole time

name: Ankle hops (hyperarch)
description: Low, fast hops off a locked-arch foot — the very first rung of the plyo ladder. Building the reactive stiffness the sport needs at minimal knee cost, with the HFT drive: the heel rises by rolling the hips forward, not by pressing down through the calf.
setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width, knees barely bent
Lock the foot into its arch first (the Hyperarch hold), ankle stiff
Let the heel rise by rolling the hips slightly forward — don't push down through the toes/calf
Hop a couple inches off that stiff spring; land forefoot-first and rebound immediately
cues: Foot stays LOCKED in its arch — land and leave on one stiff spring
Drive comes from the hips rolling forward, not from pressing the toes down
Quiet, quick contacts — think 'hot floor'; stop if landings get loud or heavy

Stop the set the moment landings lose control

Progress to side-to-side once forward/back is quiet and controlled
Stay tall and stiff through the legs, minimal ground contact

Knees track straight over the feet — especially landing on the left, no cave-in

Keep amplitude low — this is stiffness and control, not distance

Stick and hold the landing dead still for a beat

Knees track out over the feet as you catch; never let them cave

Absorb through ankle, knee, and hip; free leg tucked for balance
Hold the landing still for a full beat before the next rep

Absorb the landing with the knee tracking over the foot

Lift the hips so the body is one straight line
Stack the top hip directly over the bottom
Hold; drop the knee to the floor to regress

Press the down-side floor away through the forearm

Press the hands straight out and resist the band's pull to rotate you

Exhale slowly through the nose and let the belly soften
Repeat with a long, unhurried rhythm

name: Single-leg balance on bosu (dome up)
description: Single-leg balance on the bosu dome. The surface will not hold still, so the foot and hip fire continuously to keep you centred — the sensory base, dialled up.

Find the tripod and a fixed point to look at
Let the ankle make small, fast corrections rather than big saves
Progress by closing the eyes or adding a head turn

Step the centre of the platform under your arch; balance on two feet first
Lift to one leg, eyes on a fixed point

name: Oscillating KB anti-sway hold
description: Hold a light band in both hands with a kettlebell dangling from its centre, arms outstretched. The swinging bell feeds unpredictable perturbation that the trunk, hips and feet have to damp. Layer it onto any stance or surface to taste.
setup: Hold a light band in both hands; hang a light KB (~15 lb) from its centre
Extend the arms out in front, tall and braced
Let the bell start to sway — then work to make the swing die out

Stand tall and brace; keep the bell dead-still
Progress to single-leg stance or a half-kneel

Ribs down, quiet feet, arch locked
Breathe — stability, not a max effort

description: Lie back with the upper back on the ball and the feet braced low on the wall for a fixed anchor, then drive slow bodyweight trunk rotations side to side. The ball is the unstable fulcrum under the spine; the braced feet are what you fire against. No momentum, no release.

Plant both feet low against the wall baseboard — that's your fixed anchor
Arms crossed on the chest (bodyweight only), pelvis level
Rotate the ribcage slowly to one side and control the stop, then the other

description: Balanced on one planted leg with the other leg straight out to the side and the inside of that foot resting on the ball, arms overhead — slowly rotate the resting leg until the toes point straight up, then control it back. Standing end-range hip internal/external rotation trained on a single-leg base: the rotation you leak on every cut, upright and sport-shaped.
setup: Stand tall on one leg, the other leg straight out to the side
Rest the inside of the raised foot on top of the ball, arms reaching overhead
In a controlled manner, rotate the whole leg so the foot turns until the toes point straight up
Return under control and repeat; keep the stance hip quiet
cues: The rotation happens at the hip — turn the leg, don't just roll the ball
Stay tall through the overhead arms; don't let the trunk collapse toward the ball
Own a small clean range before chasing toes-straight-up

name: Isometric push-up hold
description: A mid-range push-up held with intent — not a passive plank. Actively pull the hands into the floor (engaging biceps, lats and shoulders) while the chest lengthens. The Schroeder/Archuleta upper-body iso base: own the position before the explosiveness.
setup: Set up in the bottom third of a push-up, elbows ~90 degrees, body one line
Actively pull the hands toward each other / into the floor — grip the ground
Brace the trunk and glutes; shoulders down and back
Hold with full intent; breathe steadily
cues: Pull the hands into the floor the whole time — intent, not a passive hold
Long line head-to-heel; ribs down, glutes on
Relax the face; keep the tension everywhere else
Regress to knees or a higher surface to keep the position clean

name: Overhead isometric hold
description: Holding a weight locked out overhead (or pressing up into rack pins) — a shoulder-stability and pressing iso. Owns the overhead position the push jerk later expresses explosively.
setup: Press a manageable weight to lockout overhead (or press up into a rack pin)
Stack wrist over elbow over shoulder; ribs down
Squeeze the glutes and brace — no low-back arch
Hold the position still with intent
cues: Actively push TALL into the weight — reach the ceiling
Ribs down, no arching the low back
Shoulders packed; biceps by the ears
Keep it a weight you fully control

name: Speed bench press
description: Submaximal bench pressed with maximal speed — the Archuleta signature (he pressed with a sub-quarter-second concentric). Load stays light (~50-60%); every rep is a fast, intent-driven push, no grinding, no bar release (no-throw).
setup: Load ~50-60% of a hard single — speed, not max
Lower under control to a light chest touch
Drive the bar up as FAST as possible — accelerate all the way
Rack and reset crisp; end the set when bar speed drops
cues: Every rep is maximal intent to MOVE FAST, not to grind
Light load — if a rep slows, the set is over
Control the lower, explode the up
Never release the bar (no-throw) — speed pressing, not a throw

name: Chin-up flexed-arm hold
description: Holding the top (or a strong mid-range) of a chin-up — the pulling iso for back and biceps, intent-driven: keep actively pulling higher into the bar even when nothing is moving. The pull-side base under the explosive row.
setup: Pull to the top of a chin-up (chin over bar) or a strong mid-range
Hold with the elbows driving down and back
Shoulders down, away from the ears; ribs down
Use a band or foot assist to keep the position strong
cues: Keep actively pulling UP into the bar — intent, not a dead hang
Elbows drive down toward the ribs; squeeze the back
Shoulders packed, no shrug
Assist with a band/foot so the hold stays clean

name: Explosive band row
description: A horizontal row pulled explosively fast and returned slowly — speed strength for the back and biceps with no impact and no release (no-throw-friendly). The pulling counterpart to the speed bench.
setup: Anchor a band in front at chest height; hold with arms extended
Tall athletic posture, shoulders down
Pull the handles to the ribs as FAST as possible
Return slowly under control; reset each rep crisp
cues: Explode the pull — maximal speed to the ribs
Slow, controlled return
Squeeze the shoulder blades; elbows drive back
Tall posture — no leaning or jerking the torso

name: Plyometric push-up
description: An explosive push-up where the hands leave the floor and you catch soft — upper-body plyometrics, the push expression on top of the iso base. Earns in once the iso push-up hold is strong and the shoulders are symptom-free.
setup: Start in a strong braced push-up position
Lower under control, then drive up explosively so the hands leave the floor
Catch soft — absorb into the next rep
Reset the position; quality over quantity
cues: Explode UP — push the floor away hard
Soft, controlled catch — no collapsing at the bottom
Body stays one rigid line — no sagging hips
End the set the moment the push or catch loses quality

name: Push jerk (explosive press)
description: A dip-and-drive explosive overhead press — the legs launch the weight, the arms finish and catch it locked out. Ballistic overhead power with no release (no-throw). The explosive expression of the overhead iso hold.
setup: Hold the weight at the shoulders, tall athletic stance
Quick shallow dip at the knees, then drive explosively through the legs
Punch the weight to lockout overhead as the legs extend
Catch it stable overhead; reset to the shoulders under control
cues: Power comes from the legs — launch it, the arms finish
Catch tall and stable, ribs down, no low-back arch
Crisp and explosive; reset each rep
Never release the weight (no-throw)

name: Explosive pull-up
description: A pull-up driven as fast as possible — chest to the bar, or the hands leaving the bar at the top with a soft re-grip. The pulling plyometric: the explosive expression of the chin hold, earned once the hold is strong and the shoulders/elbows are symptom-free.
setup: Hang from the bar, shoulders packed, core braced
Pull explosively — drive the chest to the bar as fast as possible
At the top, squeeze hard (or let the hands leave and re-grip softly)
Lower under control; reset each rep crisp
cues: Maximal speed on the pull — explode up
Shoulders down and back before each rep — no dead-hang yank
Soft, controlled catch/return — protect the elbows
End the set the moment speed or control drops

name: Speed curl (biceps)
description: A biceps curl driven up fast and lowered slow — speed strength for the elbow flexors to complement the pulling work, no impact and no release. Keeps the biceps strong under the chin/pull work above it.
setup: Stand tall, weight at the thighs, elbows pinned to the sides
Curl up as FAST as possible — explosive concentric
Lower slowly under control (2-3 counts)
Keep the elbows still; no swinging or leaning
cues: Explode the lift, control the lower
Elbows pinned — no swinging the torso
Full but controlled range
Pick a weight you can move FAST for every rep

name: Deltoid raise (lateral & front)
description: Lateral and front raises for the deltoids — the direct shoulder work that rounds out the pressing. Light load, strict form, a slow controlled raise and lower. Also drives well off band handles (as you’ve been doing on the bosu during the oscillating-KB anti-sway).
setup: Stand tall, light DBs or band handles at the sides
Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height (lateral), controlled
Lower slowly, then raise to the front to shoulder height (front)
Soft elbow; no shrugging or swinging
cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands; no shrug
Slow and strict — light load, let the delts do the work
Stop each raise at shoulder height
Ribs down; don’t lean back to cheat

name: Rear-delt raise (reverse fly)
description: A bent-over reverse fly for the rear deltoids and upper back — the balancing shoulder work that keeps all the pressing from rounding you forward. Light, strict, squeeze the shoulder blades.
setup: Hinge forward (or lie chest-down on an incline), light DBs hanging
Raise the arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top
Lower slowly under control
cues: Lead with the elbows; feel the rear delts and mid-back
No swinging or momentum — strict
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
Neck long, don’t crane
